pr_title: Ensure `joy_connection_changed` is emitted on the main thread
pr_body:
Closes #78531 (once cherry-picked for `3.x`)

On Linux, the code for querying joypad status runs in a thread (`JoypadLinux::joypad_events_thread_run`). Therefore, the `joy_connection_changed` signal is not emitted on the main thread, which depending on user code, can lead do a deadlock due to thread-unsafe API.

issue_context.title: Engine freezes when calling Sprite.new() from joy_connection_changed callback
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.5.stable.official [991bb6ac7]

### System information

Debian 11 - Intel Ivybridge Mobile - GLES3

### Issue description

Pretty much what the title says, the engine freezes when I call Sprite.new() from a method that I previously connected to `joy_connection_changed` signal. No errors are shown.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the minimal reproduction project, you will see the Godot icon moving around.
2. Connect or disconnect a gamepad and you will see the icon stops moving due to engine freeze.

### Minimal reproduction project

[minimal-reproduction-project.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11821885/minimal-reproduction-project.zip)
comments:
I recall having a similar issue on my addon, which required a hack to bypass (waiting a frame):
https://github.com/rsubtil/controller_icons/blob/db639c0288e3992c6f861b4f91041adfb5a2e2f4/addons/controller_icons/ControllerIcons.gd#L102-L111
This happened on Godot 3, but I never tested if it still happens on Godot 4. I can try to see what's going on.

In the meantime, to prevent this, you can yield for a frame:
```gdscript
func _on_joy_connection_changed(device, connected):
    yield(get_tree(), "idle_frame")
    # Now run your code, it should not freeze anymore
```

review_comments: I'd add a comment to clarify, like "Defer to emit on the main thread." (IIUC).

BTW I'm not good with multithreading, but would deferring the call to `joy_connection_changed` in the Linux input code solve the issue similarly?

If only some platforms do this in a thread, maybe they should be responsible for deferring to the main thread where needed?

Though this one claims to be thread-safe so I guess this helps provide this guarantee?

Yeah, from what I've checked it seems only Linux runs on a thread, and I did try making this change there initially. But for some reason, it didn't work: on Godot 4, the signal stopped being emitted altogether; on Godot 3, the signal stopped being emitted when a joypad is disconnected, and every time I reconnected the joypad it registered a new device index.
